claim_1.claim: ELISA analysis of maternal and umbilical cord blood from 175 maternal-neonatal dyads collected at delivery showed higher anti-Spike IgG transfer ratios after first- and second-trimester vaccination than after third-trimester vaccination, with median transfer ratios of 1.5 and 1.3 versus 1.0 and p < 0.0001 for first vs third and second vs third trimester comparisons.

sources.quote: The transfer ratio (TR)—defined as the ratio of cord blood anti-Spike IgG titer to maternal anti-Spike IgG titer at delivery—was calculated for each maternal-neonatal dyad and plotted by trimester of vaccination as a metric of transfer efficiency (Fig. 5B ). This analysis revealed higher TRs generated by first and second trimester vaccination (median TR = 1.5 and 1.3) compared to third trimester vaccination (median TR = 1.0).

To further assess cord:maternal transfer ratios by trimester of vaccination, maternal and umbilical cord blood samples were collected from an additional 52 participants who delivered during the study period ( N = 175 total maternal-neonatal dyads included for this analysis). Antibodies against the SARS-CoV-2 Spike were quantified using an ELISA.

comparison.finding: higher anti-Spike IgG transfer ratio after first-trimester vaccination than after third-trimester vaccination (median transfer ratio 1.5 vs 1.0, p < 0.0001)
higher anti-Spike IgG transfer ratio after second-trimester vaccination than after third-trimester vaccination (median transfer ratio 1.3 vs 1.0, p < 0.0001)

claim_2.claim: Multiplex Bead Array Assay analysis of maternal serum from 158 vaccinated pregnant individuals showed significantly lower Spike-specific IgG1 and FcR2a/FcR2b/FcR3a binding after Ad26.COV2.S than after mRNA-1273 or BNT162b2, while the two mRNA vaccines had similar overall anti-Spike profiles except for higher IgG2 with mRNA-1273.

sources.quote: These plots reveal that whereas similar antibody profiles against Spike were observed for the two mRNA vaccines (mRNA-1273 and BNT162b2), vaccine-induced antibody titers and FcR-binding across all IgG subclasses and two antibody isotypes (IgG and IgA) were significantly lower in individuals who received the Ad26.COV2.S vaccine.

Overall, the anti-Spike response was similar in individuals who received the mRNA vaccines mRNA-1273 and BNT162b2, with the exception of a significantly higher IgG2 anti-Spike response in women vaccinated with mRNA-1273 compared to those vaccinated with BNT162b2 (Fig. S1A ).

Using systems serology, we profiled the vaccine-induced immune response in a cohort of 158 women who completed a COVID-19 vaccine course during pregnancy: 28 who received Ad26.COV2.S (1 dose), 61 who received mRNA-1273 (2 doses), and 69 who received BNT162b2 (2 doses).
A multiplexed Luminex assay was used to determine the relative concentration of antigen-specific antibody isotype and subclass titer and Fc receptor binding.

comparison.finding: Spike-specific IgG1 and FcR2a/FcR2b/FcR3a binding were significantly lower after Ad26.COV2.S than after mRNA-1273.
Spike-specific IgG1 and FcR2a/FcR2b/FcR3a binding were significantly lower after Ad26.COV2.S than after BNT162b2.
Overall anti-Spike profiles were similar between mRNA-1273 and BNT162b2, except for higher IgG2 anti-Spike response with mRNA-1273.

claim_3.claim: Pseudovirus Neutralization Assay analysis of serum from a representative subset of 70 maternal participants sampled at least 2 weeks after the single Ad26.COV2.S dose or at least 2 weeks after the second mRNA vaccine dose showed Omicron neutralizing antibodies in a greater proportion of mRNA-1273 and BNT162b2 recipients than Ad26.COV2.S recipients, although the difference was not significant (52% [13/25], 35% [12/34], and 18% [2/11], p = 0.13).

sources.quote: We found those mRNA vaccines induced neutralizing antibodies in a greater proportion of pregnant individuals than did the Ad26.COV2.S vaccine, although this difference did not reach statistical significance (52% (13/25) for mRNA-1273, 35% (12/34) for BNT162b2, 18% (2/11) for Ad26.COV2.S, p = 0.13, Fig. S2B ).

To assess the ability of maternal vaccination to generate neutralizing antibodies, we measured neutralizing activity in a representative subset of 70 maternal participants including participants vaccinated across all three trimesters ( n = 14 first trimester, 28 second trimester, 28 third trimester vaccine recipients), and with a representation of all three vaccine platforms ( n = 25 mRNA-1273, n = 34 BNT162b2, n = 11 Ad26.COV2.S).

For Ad26.COV2.S vaccine recipients, blood was collected at least 2 weeks after receiving the single vaccine dose. For mRNA-1273 and BNT162b2 vaccine recipients, blood was collected at least 2 weeks following the second vaccine dose.

comparison.finding: Omicron neutralizing antibodies were detected in a greater proportion of mRNA-1273 recipients than Ad26.COV2.S recipients (52% [13/25] vs 18% [2/11]); difference not statistically significant
Omicron neutralizing antibodies were detected in a greater proportion of BNT162b2 recipients than Ad26.COV2.S recipients (35% [12/34] vs 18% [2/11]); difference not statistically significant

claim_4.claim: Cell Mediated Immunoassay analysis of umbilical cord samples from 123 maternal-neonatal dyads showed lower Spike-specific antibody-dependent NK-cell degranulation, measured as %CD107a+ cells, in cords of Ad26.COV2.S recipients than in cords of mRNA-1273 or BNT162b2 recipients (p = 0.00085 and p = 0.006).

sources.quote: Functional antibody responses, including ADCP, ADNP, ADCD, and ADNKA (measured as % CD107a+, % MIP-1β+ and % IFNγ+ cells), were lower in the cord blood of Ad26.COV2.S recipients compared to mRNA-1273 or BNT162b2 (Fig. 3B and Fig. S 4C ).
For participants who delivered during the study time frame ( N = 123), maternal blood was drawn at the time of delivery, and umbilical cord blood was collected after delivery.
NK activity was determined as the percent of cells positive for CD107a, IFN-g or MIP-1b.

comparison.finding: lower Spike-specific antibody-dependent NK-cell degranulation, measured as %CD107a+ cells, in cords of Ad26.COV2.S recipients than in cords of mRNA-1273 recipients
lower Spike-specific antibody-dependent NK-cell degranulation, measured as %CD107a+ cells, in cords of Ad26.COV2.S recipients than in cords of BNT162b2 recipients
